children: Volvo Car held an analyst call ahead of third quarter results, and the main takeaways are mostly negative, Bernstein analysts write. Raw material inflation, weak product mix, and higher costs were already expected to hit margins in the second half, they say. But in addition, July and August volumes were exceptionally weak, particularly in China. Any sequential improvement in the EBIT margin from the 1.1% recorded in the second quarter will be difficult to achieve, and Bernstein expects guidance for breakeven free cash flow this year to be removed. Strategic initiatives will take time, and the company is already losing share to Chinese manufacturers in Europe, it says. The bank retains its underperform stock rating and cuts its target price to 16 Swedish kronor from 17 kronor. Shares fall 2.8% to 16.11 kronor. (dominic.chopping@wsj.com)
